items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: the guy that owned it happened to be a runner for Al Capone.

ctx.x: So I wanted to join the union and I knew I couldn’t get started. In those days if they caught you sitting in they’d fine you a whole bunch of money. It was terrible. They got rid of that particular group of union people. It was almost like the Spanish Inquisition, you know. Anyway, I got a job as an elevator operator in the biggest hotel, but I got elevator sick because the damn thing would go up and down. I’d get people caught in the

doors. Then I was working selling sporting goods and tobacco in a big department store. Then I went from there to a room clerk at the King Edward Hotel, which is a fancy hotel, and I stuck that out, but it was nights — 11 at night ‘til 8 in the morning. I did it for about six months. But I was determined. I never even thought about going on welfare you know, like a lot of people do today, because it was a disgrace in England to go on the dole, you wouldn’t do it. And then I wound up working in a shirt shop, and…
